questions.q: What table does a Data Policy record live on?
options: sys_data_policy2
sys_ui_policy
sys_script
sys_dictionary
questions.explain: A Data Policy is a sys_data_policy2 record, scoped to a table, with a condition and child sys_data_policy_rule records.

questions.q: What is the key practical difference between a Data Policy and a UI Policy?
options: There is no real difference; they are two names for the same mechanism
A Data Policy enforces its rule at the server level regardless of how the record is written; a UI Policy only governs the rendered form
A UI Policy can only be used on Incident records
A Data Policy can only make fields visible, never mandatory
questions.explain: That server-side, write-path-agnostic enforcement is exactly what makes a Data Policy the right tool when a rule must always hold true.

questions.q: Which two real enforcement options does a sys_data_policy_rule support?
options: Visible and hidden
Mandatory and read-only
Encrypted and audited
Archived and deleted
questions.explain: A Data Policy Rule names one field and sets it mandatory or read-only — it never controls visibility.

questions.q: What does turning on "Apply to UI" on a Data Policy actually do?
options: It disables server-side enforcement entirely
It converts the Data Policy into a UI Policy
It also mirrors the mandatory/read-only behavior onto the form, in addition to server-side enforcement
It makes the field visible or hidden based on the condition
questions.explain: Apply to UI gives the end user the same live form feedback a UI Policy would provide, while the server-side enforcement still applies regardless of that setting.

questions.q: A Data Policy makes Asset Tag mandatory whenever Category is Hardware. A Scripted REST API call creates a Hardware incident with Asset Tag blank. What happens?
options: The record saves successfully, because Data Policies only apply to form submissions
The platform rejects the write because the Data Policy is enforced at the server, independent of the write path
The API call succeeds but silently sets Asset Tag to a default value
The Data Policy is ignored unless Apply to UI is checked
questions.explain: Unlike a UI Policy, a Data Policy's rule is enforced by the platform on every write path, including a Scripted REST API call — this is exactly the gap Lesson 20 identified.
